description.value: The study investigated how positive, negative, and neutral facial affect modulate effective connectivity within a right-hemisphere prefrontal-amygdala-fusiform face area network during dynamic face matching.

design.value: Thirty-three healthy volunteers completed a 6-min dynamic face-matching and shape-matching fMRI task with alternating face and shape blocks. Whole-brain GLM analyses were followed by dynamic causal modeling, random-effects Bayesian model comparison, Bayesian model averaging, and connectivity-behavior correlations.

source_definition.value: positive, negative, and neutral valence conditions
the six realignment parameters derived from preprocessing

medical_condition.value: No subject reported any past or current psychiatric disorder.

task_description.value: Participants were presented with triplets of emotional faces and shapes and matched the dynamic target image with one of two static probe images by emotion or number of vertices.

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed to match either the left or the right static item at the bottom with the dynamic item on top and to press either the left or the right button with their dominant hand on a response-pad to indicate their choice as soon as they recognized which probe matched.

stimuli.value: Face images from the Radboud face database, including faces of 38 white actors; positive blocks included happy, surprised, and neutral faces, negative blocks included sad and disgusted faces, and neutral blocks included neutral and surprised faces. Shapes were polygons superimposed to a whirled face.

instrument.value: Philips Achieva 3 Tesla scanner (Philips Medical Systems) using a 32-channel head coil

description.value: Functional images were acquired with a multiband echoplanar images (EPIs) sequence, 15° tilted downwards of AC-PC, 54 slices, matrix size 96 × 94 px, flip angle 80°, no gap, SENSE-factor 2, and MB-factor 2. Five dummy scans were acquired before the actual data acquisition.

description.value: Preprocessing included slice-timing correction, realignment, coregistration, segmentation, normalization to MNI-152 template space using deformations derived from segmentation, resampling to 2-mm isometric voxels, and smoothing with a 6-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel.

model_settings.value: The final GLM included regressors for all faces, positive faces, negative faces, neutral faces, and shapes, plus six realignment parameters as nuisance regressors.

estimator.value: one-sample t test and second-level repeated measures ANOVA

model_settings.value: The model included four regions: LPFC, MPFC, AMY, and FFA. The model space contained 256 models with bidirectional intrinsic connections between MPFC and AMY, MPFC and LPFC, FFA and LPFC, and FFA and AMY, and systematically varied valence modulation across connections between MPFC and LPFC and MPFC and AMY.

estimator.value: random-effects family-wise Bayesian model selection and Bayesian model averaging

description.value: Positive blocks included happy, surprised and neutral faces, forming overall positively valenced stimulus triplets.
Negative blocks used sad and disgusted faces.
Neutral blocks used neutral and surprised faces, with neutral dynamic target stimuli morphed to surprised emotion from 0% to 30% intensity and back to 0% intensity.
During the shape-matching task, the target shape was morphed from a round circle into a polygon with three to eight vertices.

interpretations.value: The dynamic face-matching and shape-matching task showed a significant effect of task in brain regions commonly recruited during face processing.

definition.value: a main effect of valence across positive, negative, and neutral valence conditions

interpretations.value: The repeated measures ANOVA revealed a main effect of valence in the MPFC, the right medial temporal lobe, the superior temporal gyrus, the left medial temporal lobe, the left cerebellum, the left AMY, and the right parahippocampal gyrus.
